scope: Provenance and declared-claim gate for MicroProxy V0-V8. Functional source proofs under explicit compiler/runtime/provider/facade trust are distinct from model proofs, finite tests, historical bytecode snapshots, blocked alternate routes and deferred timing/expert work. This ledger never proves the mathematics itself.

dafny-toolchain.statement: Dafny 4.9.1 and Z3 4.12.1 implementation correctness; official archive bytes are pinned and checked.

dafny-runtime.statement: The pinned Maven DafnyRuntime 4.9.1 jar is trusted and differs from the compiler-bundled runtime; byte differences are not assumed away.

javac-jvm.statement: javac and JVM correctness, including exact class/JAR delivery; no JIT/CPU timing property is assumed.

jdk-primitives.statement: Selected JDK SHA-2/SHA-3/HMAC/AEAD/classical providers implement their documented primitives; entropy and cryptographic hardness are separate assumptions.

generated-runtime-discipline.statement: Reviewed generated-runtime/bytecode metadata boundaries hold for the pinned emitted graph; this is not a whole-program noninterference or timing theorem.

reviewed-java-facades.statement: The small handwritten Shake and ML-KEM facades are reviewed and tested adapters, not Dafny-proved code.

packet-compiler-lowering.statement: The packet component trusts exactly two documented bounded-shift compiler lowerings; all other compiler output is not rewritten.

saw-toolchain.statement: SAW/Crucible bytecode semantics/translation, Cryptol, the bundled solver and the selected JDK class-file model are trusted.

lean-toolchain.statement: Lean 4.35.0 kernel checking and the explicitly allowed standard axioms are trusted; untrusted axioms/holes/native evaluation are rejected by the runner.

tlc-finite-model.statement: TLC exhaustively explores only the configured finite caps; this is bounded model checking, not unbounded refinement.

crypto-hardness-entropy.statement: Cryptographic hardness, PRF/PRP/entropy and security reductions are assumptions; functional proofs do not imply them.

jvm-timing-jit-cpu-gc.statement: HotSpot/JIT, CPU, GC, provider and physical-erasure timing are outside the proofs; local samples are observations, not a constant-time theorem.

trusted-bytecode-mapper-policy.statement: The javap-based extractor, CFG/taint/dispatch policy mapping and certificate emitter are trusted reviewed code, mutation-tested but not formally verified; certificate semantics are not JVM value/timing semantics.

assumed-owned-helper-trace-contracts.statement: The five checked caller certificates assume 19 opaque owned helper/adapter trace contracts; every assumed target remains in the unchecked-owned inventory and is not a provider or proved callee.

obligations.statement: The local Dafny HKDF kernel is a scoped functional implementation proof over its general public domain relative to deterministic external HMAC, with exact generated-source/class/production binding, 10/10 rejected controls and two 45-case/2766-assertion JDK result records. The V1 milestone remains partial because the pinned AWS full dependency-closure replay failed; target-only success is not closure.

The local standalone kernel is independently specified and verified; AWS provenance is attribution for reused recurrence structure, not a full upstream graph replay.

The pinned local replay has 21 kernel checks, 22 general-domain checks, 10/10 rejected controls and two 45-case/2766-assertion JDK runs; these are finite checks supplemented by a source proof, not a Java adapter refinement theorem.
The only Dafny assumption is deterministic external HMAC with fixed output length.
JCE/HMAC correctness, Java adapters, compiler/runtime and JVM execution remain trusted boundaries.
No cryptographic security reduction, constant-time trace or physical erasure is claimed.
Compatibility extensions (short nonempty PRKs, empty label suffix) are accepted by the API contract.
